newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Crown recovers as Swedish bond yields rise.
newsitem.headline: Crown recovers as Swedish bond yields rise.

text.p: Swedish bond yields rose in thin trade on Friday in a session driven by the U.S. market.
The crown weakened versus the mark, but recovered to end the session slightly stronger at 4.4410 compared to 4.4500 Thursday.
Some dealers said Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, probably sold marks on Friday as the crown weakened starting at the level of 4.4630 crowns per mark.
"There is no fundamental weakness and the Riksbank probably wanted to nudge the market and advise to to cool down," one chief dealer said.
"It's no surprise that bank is in," he added.
Flows in crown trade were small, however.
"We have to wait until companies start up again after the holidays see if the crown is generally or temporarily weak," one dealer said.
The market was expecting no repo rate cut on Tuesday, according to a Reuter survey. Analysts said the Riksbank would await the December inflation figures due on January 21.
Six-month T-bill rates closed unchanged at 3.80 percent and ten-year bond yields rose four basis points to 6.86 percent.
The spread between German and Swedish long yields dropped two basis points to 88.
